feedback.finish: Wetland biomes are flat areas covered in shallow water. They are usually a type of freshwater biome, but can also be saltwater when they are near the coast.

instruction.text: Read the description and select the correct type of wetland.

atoms.a: A swamp is a wetland in a forest. There are lots of trees here.
Marshes are areas of shallow water with grasses and reeds. They are often found along the edges of lakes or rivers.
A bog is a freshwater wetland with soft, spongy ground that is mostly made of decaying plant matter called peat.

instruction.text: Wetland biomes are home to a variety of wildlife, which all have adaptations to best survive in their habitat. Select the correct answer.

atoms.a: What are the two ways in which otters have adapted to wetlands?
b: ++ability to close their nostrils and eyes

feedback.finish: Their webbed feet help them to paddle in the water, and the ability to close their nostrils and ears prevents water from entering while they swim.

instruction.text: Select the pin on the map.

feedback.end: This is the county of Somerset. Here you can find a large area of wetland called the Somerset Levels.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: The Somerset Levels is one of the lowest areas in the UK. It was once covered by the sea, but today it is a vast landscape of marshes and bogs with rivers running throughout.
These rivers often burst their banks in winter months and cause the entire wetland to flood, which affects many of the surrounding villages and farms.
Local authorities have tried to lessen the flooding for years by draining the water from the wetland, but high rainfall can still cause floods there.

atoms.a: What type of wetlands are found in the Somerset Levels?
What causes flooding in the Somerset Levels?
How have local authorities tried to prevent this flooding?
